comment: East of the square: Lamplight Lane, the Little Post Office, the Waiting House and the Lamp House above it, the Lantern Bridge, the river's edge, the Dusk Road, and the Hill of Long Shadows.

rooms.title: Lamplight Lane
rooms.seed: a narrow cobbled lane of hanging lanterns winding between leaning houses with blue doors and window boxes of moss, dusk light pooling between them
rooms.description: Lanterns hang on brackets all along the narrow lane, and the leaning houses have blue doors and window boxes full of moss. The square is back west. A little post office sits to the north, a tall crooked house with a lit front window stands east, and the lane runs south down to a bridge.

rooms.title: The Little Post Office
rooms.seed: a tiny post office crammed floor to ceiling with wooden pigeonholes, each holding letters that were written and never sent, a brass bell on a worn counter, a stove, a basket of string
rooms.description: Wooden pigeonholes climb every wall, and every pigeonhole holds letters: written, sealed, and never sent. A brass bell sits on the worn counter beside a basket of string. The little stove keeps the paper dry. The lane is south.

variants: You tap the brass bell on the counter. Ting! Fen looks up at once, pencil already out. 'Post, or only saying hello? Both are welcome at this counter.'
Ting. Fen finishes the address she is writing before she looks up. 'Heard you the first time,' she says, pleased. 'The bell likes being rung. Not many people think to.'
do.others: {actor} taps the brass bell on the counter. Ting!

do.text: You tap the brass bell on the counter. Ting! It rings bright and small, the way it does when a letter finds its door.
do.others: {actor} taps the brass bell on the counter. Ting!

rooms.title: The Waiting House
rooms.seed: the warm front room of a tall crooked house where lost hours rest while they wait, mismatched armchairs, a kettle always on the hob, a board of brass room keys by the stair
rooms.description: Mismatched armchairs crowd the warm front room, and a kettle mutters on the hob. By the stair hangs a board of brass room keys, one for every hour waiting to go home. It smells of tea and clean linen. The lane is west; a steep stair climbs to a little room under the roof.

variants: You sink into one of the mismatched armchairs. It is exactly as soft as it looks, and the kettle mutters approvingly.
You take the armchair nearest the stair, and the room settles around you like a cat round a warm spot.
do.others: {actor} sinks into one of the mismatched armchairs.

do.text: Linden laughs. 'Nothing to eat, pet, I don't bake. But there's tea, and there's always tea.'
Linden has a cup in your hands before you've finished asking: bergamot, a little honey-coloured, and hot right through.
do.others: Linden puts a cup of tea into {actor}'s hands.

rooms.title: The Lamp House
rooms.seed: a cozy slant-roofed attic bedroom at dusk, bundles of lamp wicks hanging from wooden rafters, folded paper lanterns stacked on shelves, a narrow bed with a patchwork quilt under a small west window, a butter-yellow scarf on a hook
rooms.description: Spare wicks hang in bundles from the rafters, and folded paper lantern-skins lean in stacks like sleeping moths. A narrow bed faces the west window, where the sun goes down; nothing in the room faces east. The stair goes down to the Waiting House.

do.text: Bell is already asleep in the narrow bed, one sooty hand trailing off the quilt. It isn't yours to sleep in, and there's no room besides.
You sit on the edge of the narrow bed, and think better of it. This is Bell's bed, facing Bell's west window, and it isn't yours to sleep in.

glimpsed.text: The folded skins in the stacks are Bell's, each waiting for its own lantern. A spare sometimes turns up by dusk, when one is truly needed.
The folded skins in the stacks are Bell's, each waiting for its own lantern, and you leave the stacks as they lean.
The wicks are Bell's spares, hung in bundles from the rafters against the lanterns' long nights, and they stay where Bell can reach them.

rooms.title: The Lantern Bridge
rooms.seed: an arched stone bridge hung with lanterns over a slow dark river, their reflections swaying on the water like slow golden fish
rooms.description: The old stone bridge arches over a slow dark river, hung end to end with lanterns whose reflections sway on the water like golden fish. The lane climbs north back into the village; the road runs south into a wide meadow; worn steps lead down to the water's edge.

rooms.title: The Slow River's Edge
rooms.seed: a reedy riverbank below a lantern-hung bridge where a wide river moves as slowly as an afternoon, lantern-light trembling on the water
rooms.description: Reeds whisper along the bank, and the river goes by as slowly as a long afternoon. Lantern-light from the bridge trembles on the water. Now and then something small and bright turns over under the surface and is gone. Steps lead up to the bridge.

variants: You listen to the river. It says the same long word over and over, and never seems to reach the end of it.
You listen. Reeds brush together, and somewhere a fish turns over with a sound like a page.
You listen to the water go by, slow as a Sunday, and feel your shoulders come down a little.

rooms.title: The Dusk Road
rooms.seed: a long meadow road under a wide dusk sky where small lights drift down like slow snow, the long grass silver-green, a wide catcher's net leaning on a fence post
rooms.description: The road runs long and pale through a meadow of silver-green grass, under the widest sky in the dream. At dusk small lights drift down here like slow snow: hours, the villagers say, coming to rest. A wide soft net leans on a fence post. The bridge is north; a hill rises east.

do.text: You stand still in the long grass and wait, the way Sorrel does. The small lights drift down around you like slow snow, and one of them turns aside, as if it had been looking for you.
do.others: {actor} stands very still in the long grass, and a small light drifts down into their cupped hands.

variants: You stand still in the long grass. The small lights drift down around you like slow snow, and a few settle on the net by the fence post, softly, where Sorrel will find them.
You wait, and the lights come down, and every one of them takes its time. So do you.

do.text: You wait in the long grass. The sky is only sky just now; the lights come down at dusk, Sorrel says, to anyone who stands still.

glimpsed.text: The small lights drift down past your fingers like slow snow and settle where they will. They come, Sorrel says, to anyone who stands still.
The small lights drift past your fingers like slow snow, on their way to wherever hours go to rest.
There are no lights just now. They drift down at dusk, the villagers say, like slow snow.

rooms.title: The Hill of Long Shadows
rooms.seed: the highest place in a dream village, a round grassy hill with one weathered bench, looking east over rooftops and meadow toward a pale edge of sky
rooms.description: From the top of the hill you can see the whole village: the clocktower, the lanterns, the river's slow shine. One weathered bench faces east, toward a pale edge of sky that never quite decides to become morning while anyone is watching. The Dusk Road is back to the west.

do.text: You sit on the weathered bench, facing east, and the turned-back clock gives one hopeful tick in your pocket. This might be the place to spend an hour, on purpose.
do.others: {actor} sits on the weathered bench, facing east.

variants: You sit on the weathered bench, facing east. The pale edge of the sky considers you, and decides nothing yet.
You sit on the bench with the little sun carved in one arm and the lantern in the other. Below, the whole village keeps its time, and none of it needs you just now.
do.others: {actor} sits on the weathered bench, facing east.

things.name: pigeonholes
things.seed: wooden pigeonholes labeled in Fen's tidy hand (TO THE ONE WHO LIGHTS THE LAMPS, TO WHOEVER FINDS THIS, TO MY SISTER, TO ME, LATER), each holding a few soft letters

variants: You ease one letter an inch out of the pigeonhole marked TO WHOEVER FINDS THIS: sealed, soft with handling, addressed in a careful round hand. Fen clears her throat, kindly, and you slide it back. Unsent letters are read by the ones they're meant for.
You run a finger along the letters in TO MY SISTER. Every one is sealed. 'Fronts only, in this office,' Fen says, not unkindly, and you let them be.

things.name: brass bell
things.seed: a small brass bell on the counter, polished bright where a thousand palms have tapped it

things.name: kettle
things.seed: a copper kettle muttering on the hob, never quite boiling and never quite cold, as if it knows someone will want tea in a minute

things.name: board of room keys
things.seed: a board of little brass keys on hooks, each hook labeled in chalk with the name of an hour waiting to go home

roster.text: Chalked on the hooks, in Linden's round hand: {waiting}. Wiped clean, the hours gone home or kept: {home}.
roster.empty: Every hook is chalked clean; no hour is waiting just now.

things.name: catcher's net
things.seed: a wide net of soft grey thread on a long ash pole, so fine it seems to be made of evening; it belongs to Sorrel

things.name: weathered bench
things.seed: a weathered wooden bench facing east, its slats worn smooth; someone has carved a tiny sun into one arm, and a lantern into the other

things.name: west window
things.seed: a small window over the narrow bed, facing west; through it the sun goes down behind the rooftops, slow and gold, as if it were saying goodnight to this one room in particular
